teaser: Three days of blood turned out to be three days of rust: the leaves were asking for iron in the water, and only a seven-year-old could see the dash that said so. Hesper has a new rule, no one opens a hand on an adult's reading again, and a new problem: the shape Bea copied at dusk is the flowering sign, the one that came nine years ago and cost a dead child her name. The plant is about to ask for a name, and no one on the farm is allowed to remember the last one.
